summary:
Radar for 2026-11-20 (GLP-1 focus). Three things are happening at once.

(1) The approved-pill story is accelerating. Health Canada authorised Foundayo (orforglipron) on Nov 13, with pharmacy supply expected in January. The TGA registered it in Australia on Nov 16. The Wegovy pill was also approved in Australia. That is fresh demand from Canadian and Australian viewers on top of US searches for "foundayo vs wegovy pill". Our Foundayo video already gains about 30 minutes a day, so the queued Foundayo what-to-expect long video (after the fact-check fixes) is the top pick. A label-based comparison of the pill with tirzepatide injections is a strong follow-up.

(2) Thanksgiving is in 6 days. Holiday-table and pen-travel Shorts are at their peak. The Conversation (Nov 19) and Newswise (Nov 20) both ran GLP-1 holiday guides.

(3) The class-wide NAION label change is now in mainstream news: FDA order Nov 9, ABC Nov 18, and the Denmark compensation story Nov 19. That is the hook for the queued Serious Risks long video and a calm "sudden vision change" Short.

The broad evergreen questions still win: weight loss in the trials (refreshed by ScienceDaily's "why don't they work for everyone"), stopping and keeping results (Healthline Nov 19), plus the felt-symptom Shorts (nausea, hair loss, injection sites).

Fresh randomized science is either pipeline or out of our population, so it goes in with caution:
- retatrutide TRIUMPH-4 knee pain (NEJM) and TRANSCEND-T2D-2 against semaglutide
- SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS in JAMA (teens)
- the semaglutide binge-eating RCT (Penn)

None of these is a head-to-head against tirzepatide in an obesity population, so none triggers the 48-hour fast-turn rule.

Rejected: Shorts on Wegovy in 6–11-year-olds framed around a "troubling side effect", psychosis after stopping (case reports), and compounded or telehealth seller stories. Also out: the Florida no-prescription seller, the GLP-1 vacation, employer coverage and cost, and celebrity sex-life stories.

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill: what to expect from the label, now approved in Canada (Health Canada, Nov 13; in pharmacies from January) and Australia (TGA, Nov 16)
candidates.angle: Approved-drug what-to-expect long video: how the pill differs from weekly tirzepatide injections, what the label's Trial 1 (in adults without diabetes) showed, common adverse events (GI, mostly during dose escalation), and what to ask your prescriber. Apply all of the 11-20 fact-check fixes: 'adverse events' wording, 'weight-related' kept in the population, 17.2 mg top label dose with −11.1%, your own history of MTC/MEN 2. No dosing.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–14 days (Canadian and Australian launch coverage through January)
candidates.why_now: Two new national approvals in a week, with mainstream coverage in Canada (CTV, Global, CityNews) and Australia (AusDoc, RACGP newsGP, Medical Republic). Our existing Foundayo video already gains about 30 minutes a day from 'foundayo' searches, which proves the demand. Approved-drug search is one of our two proven earners.

evidence.signal: Health Canada authorised Foundayo on Nov 13; Lilly expects pharmacy availability in January
Doctors can now prescribe Australia's second oral GLP-1 (Nov 18)
Canadian product page for Foundayo

candidates.topic: Foundayo pill vs Wegovy pill vs tirzepatide injection: what the labels and separate trials show (no head-to-head trial)
candidates.angle: Approved-drug comparison anchored on tirzepatide: how you take each one (with or without food vs an empty stomach), average weight loss in each drug's own obesity trial (named as separate trials, not a direct comparison), and the common GI adverse events. Frame it as questions to bring to your prescriber. US labels first, with an AU/CA note. Never rank them as 'best', and give no switching advice.

candidates.why_now: The Australian (Nov 20) asked 'Are the new GLP-1 weight-loss pills as effective as Ozempic?' and News.com.au ran two pill stories the same day. Web competition is heavy (Noom, Ro, SingleCare, Superdrug), but most of it is telehealth marketing. A neutral, label-based YouTube explainer anchored on tirzepatide is still thin.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and the new NAION eye warning: what the label change says, how rare it is, and which sudden vision changes need urgent care
candidates.angle: Label-change search-demand Short, plus a chapter in Serious Risks. The FDA's pooled-trial rate is 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years (15 probable events across 126 trials and 134,253 people). Sudden painless vision loss in one eye means urgent care. Name both NANOS and the AAO. Never use the observational 8.9% vs 1.8% figure as the headline.
candidates.why_now: The FDA's class-wide order (Nov 9) reached ABC News on Nov 18. Medical Daily (Nov 19) paired it with Denmark compensating 31 users. A label-change topic of the kind that beat channel averages 10–195x in this niche, and it was 471 views on TikTok for us.

Pancreatitis 0.23 vs 0.11 per 100 years only alongside the weight-trial 0.14 vs 0.15. Name the warning 'Suicidal Behavior and Ideation'. Cite the real Medication Guide URL. Answer the 'hidden risk' headlines without fear.
